text:
rory: Noticing a spike in failed EU warm-pool joins starting ~07:12. Nodes can't reach KMS and some assume-role denies. Staging and prod eu-west-1 affected.
tanvi: Logs from node-init show connection timed out to kms endpoint, and NAT gateway errors. Example: 
```
2026-03-22T07:13:04Z node-init ERROR http: Get https://kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/: dial tcp 52.16.0.0:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-22T07:13:05Z aws-nat ERROR natgw: 503 ServiceUnavailable
```
sam: Confirmed. Firewall/team rolled out a default-deny egress NACL update at 07:05 that blocks 443 outbound to public endpoints except a small allowlist. KMS IP ranges weren't included.
oncall-sre: Autoscaler reacted by launching nodes in us-west-2 to meet capacity. We're seeing a cross-region egress increase and token-billing spikes.
ops-bot: Deploy-log: "nacl-egress-lockdown:apply" (07:05) by security. Change request CR-2026-401 created.
security: The lockdown was meant for data exfil prevention, but we scoped to only managed services. Looks like the warmpool boot relies on KMS public API IPs which are dynamic.
leah: Theres also an IAM AssumeRole condition change last week that tightened source VPC checks for the provisioning role. Some of the failing nodes show AccessDenied after retries. So we might have dual failure: network + IAM.
finance: FYI, cross-region fallbacks have added ~€4.2k in egress/instance costs so far this morning. If we keep spinning in us-west-2 at current rates it's ~€10k/day.
rory: Immediate plan: (A) add KMS IP ranges to NACL/allowlist for eu-west-1 (B) temporarily open egress to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com via FQDN proxy (C) roll back the AssumeRole sourceVPC condition for the provisioning role while we validate. Which one is fastest?
tanvi: (A) is fastest but brittle. AWS publishes kms endpoints with large prefixes. (B) is safer if we can proxy DNS at edge — we have a sidecar proxy in warmpool agent?
oncall-sre: We can push a targeted NACL allow for the current known KMS CIDRs for the immediate 30m window. I'll queue it if security concurs.
security: Approve targeted limited NACL allow for KMS prefixes in eu-west-1 for 45 minutes. Need change note and link to incident. We'll not relax AssumeRole yet.
sam: While that's happening, we can also change the node bootstrap to use the internal KMS VPC endpoint (we already have one in the region but warmpool subnets weren't using it). Patch ready: set AWS_KMS_ENDPOINT to https://kms-vpc.internal.local.
leah: That patch will avoid public egress entirely. But deployment takes ~2 hours due to canary windows. So short-term NACL allow + route change for current warmpool runs.
ops-bot: Change request CR-2026-402 created (temporary NACL allow for KMS prefixes, expires 2026-03-22T08:00Z). Requires security and oncall-sre approval.
oncall-sre: Applied NACL allow @07:25. Monitoring shows node-init connections succeeding now. Warm pool join errors dropping.
leah: IAM still had a handful of AccessDenied traces. Looks like some instance profiles use an older role ARN after a deploy on 03/20. I'll open a tiny KMS key policy patch to add the legacy role for decrypt only.
security: Make it constrained to decrypt action and only for that single legacy role ARN. Include audit annotation.
rory: Good. Follow-ups: make warmpool bootstrap prefer VPC KMS endpoint, add canary test that runs with tightened AssumeRole+NACL to catch regressions, and add a check to policy PRs to enumerate bootstrap external dependencies (KMS, STS, etc.).
finance: Also recommend a temporary budget rule and alert at €6k/day to avoid surprise billing if autoscaler flails. I'll raise a chargeback notification to the product teams consuming warm-pool capacity.
tanvi: Metrics update at 07:45: warmpool_join_failures: 142 -> 12, cross_region_instances_started: 18 -> 18 (further launches prevented). Estimated remaining daily delta: ~€1.3k (mostly already incurred).
leah: Opening tickets: INFRA-1901 (kms-vpc-endpoint-default-for-warmpool), INFRA-1902 (bootstrap-iam-arn-hygiene), INFRA-1903 (canary-policy-before-iam-PR).
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-601 severity P2 owner rory.
security: We'll add a short audit query to find any other services with public KMS dependency and report back in #eng-security. Also will update PR template to require a "bootstrap dependency checklist".
oncall-sre: Closing loop for now. Warm pools back to ~95% healthy. Leaving NACL allow to expire automatically at 08:00. If anything pops, ping oncall.
rory: Thanks everyone. Postmortem: include timeline, firewall change, IAM overlap, cost impact, and the fix to prefer VPC endpoint. Let's be stricter about network change rollouts for infra-critical paths. :thumbsup:
